title: Water Level / Fill Fault
shortDescription: The washer did not reach the target water level in the allowed time.
fullDescription:
F21 is posted when the pressure sensor does not see water level rise despite the inlet valve being energised. Causes include closed taps, blocked inlet screens, or failed valves.

Fisher & Paykel top-loaders are particularly sensitive to low mains pressure on hot-only or cold-only fills.

causes.cause: Supply tap closed or partly open

fixSteps.title: Check taps
fixSteps.instruction: Open both hot and cold taps fully.

fixSteps.title: Clean filters
fixSteps.instruction: Unscrew inlet hoses and rinse mesh screens.

fixSteps.title: Replace valve
fixSteps.instruction: Fit a new dual inlet valve.

whenToCallPro: If pressure sensor itself is suspect.

faq.a: Cycles use both hot and cold; a closed hot tap still triggers F21.

title: Overflow
shortDescription: Water level exceeded the overflow pressure threshold.
fullDescription:
F22 is raised when the pressure sensor reports water above the overflow mark. A stuck-open inlet valve, a failed pressure sensor, or a blocked air dome cause it.

The drain pump runs automatically to lower the level - do not open the door during this.

fixSteps.title: Shut off water
fixSteps.instruction: Close both taps to prevent further fill.

fixSteps.title: Replace valve
fixSteps.instruction: If a valve is stuck, swap the inlet valve.

whenToCallPro: If pressure dome and hoses are hard to reach.

faq.a: Yes, it protects the floor - let it finish.

title: Drain Fault
shortDescription: Water was not removed in the allowed drain time.
fullDescription:
F26 is raised when the drain cycle fails to empty the drum. A clogged pump filter, kinked drain hose, or failed drain pump cause it.

Clean the pump filter at the base before suspecting the pump.

fixSteps.title: Clean filter
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the pump filter and clear debris.

fixSteps.title: Check hose
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure drain hose is not kinked or clogged.

fixSteps.title: Replace pump
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the drain pump if still failing.

whenToCallPro: If the machine needs to be tipped.

faq.a: Rinsing reduces debris reaching the pump filter.

title: Motor Control Fault
shortDescription: The motor control module reports a fault.
fullDescription:
E51 is posted when the motor control cannot drive the direct-drive motor as commanded. A failed control, stator winding fault, or locked drum can cause it.

Inspect for obstructions in the drum and then look to the motor control module.

fixSteps.title: Check drum
fixSteps.instruction: Turn drum by hand to check for binding or foreign objects.

fixSteps.title: Replace control
fixSteps.instruction: Swap motor control module if drum is free.

whenToCallPro: If stator or bearing replacement required.

title: Continuous Beep / Child Lock
shortDescription: The washer beeps continuously and will not respond.
fullDescription:
A continuous beep is usually not a fault - it indicates a paused cycle, child lock active, or an end-of-cycle reminder.

Press Start/Pause to resume, or hold the child lock button for 3 seconds to clear the lock.

fixSteps.title: Release child lock
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the child lock key for 3 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Resume cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Press Start/Pause to continue.

faq.a: Some models allow disabling end-of-cycle tone in settings.

title: Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Wash water NTC reads out of range.
fullDescription:
F24 appears when the NTC in the sump reads open or shorted. Heating is disabled; cold cycles may still run.

Replace the NTC near the heater element.

fixSteps.title: Access heater
fixSteps.instruction: Remove front panel.

fixSteps.title: Replace NTC
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the sensor near the heater element.

whenToCallPro: If boot gasket removal is intimidating.

faq.a: Often yes, but not hot cycles.

title: Heater Fault
shortDescription: Water did not reach target temperature in time.
fullDescription:
F25 indicates the heater failed to bring water to setpoint. Failed element, scale on the heater, or blown thermal fuse cause it.

Test heater resistance before replacement.

fixSteps.title: Test heater
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance (~25 ohm).

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Fit new heater element.

faq.a: Run hot cycles with descaler to reduce scale.

title: Door Lock Fault
shortDescription: Door lock did not confirm locked or unlocked state.
fullDescription:
F27 appears when the PTC door lock does not report the expected state. A failed lock assembly or loose harness are typical causes.

Replace the door lock; on some models it is behind the boot gasket.
symptoms: Door will not lock or unlock

fixSteps.title: Replace lock
fixSteps.instruction: Fit a new door lock assembly.

whenToCallPro: If door trapped with water inside.
videoSearchQuery: Fisher Paykel washer F27 door lock

faq.a: No - use emergency release cord at the base first.

title: User Interface Fault
fullDescription:
F10 is posted when the display board fails self-test at power-up. Often a power surge or water ingress causes it.

Power cycle first; if it persists, replace the display board.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Breaker off 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Replace display
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the UI board.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: UI and motor control are not communicating.
fullDescription:
F11 indicates a dropped serial link between UI and motor control. Loose harness or failed board cause it.

Reseat harnesses after a power cycle.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Breaker off 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Reseat
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat harnesses between UI and motor control.

title: Out of Balance
shortDescription: Load is too unbalanced to spin safely.
fullDescription:
F34 is posted when the accelerometer senses excessive drum wobble during spin-up. Bulky items, small loads, or worn suspension cause it.

Redistribute the load and restart spin; if F34 returns with balanced loads, the suspension or damper may be worn.

fixSteps.title: Redistribute
fixSteps.instruction: Rearrange laundry inside drum.

fixSteps.title: Level
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the washer is level on its feet.

fixSteps.title: Replace suspension
fixSteps.instruction: If F34 persists with balanced loads, replace shock absorbers.

faq.a: Add a few items to help balance.

title: Supply Frequency Error
shortDescription: Mains frequency is out of the expected range.
fullDescription:
F42 is posted when the control cannot detect 50 or 60 Hz stably, typically on a generator or inverter supply. It can also indicate a failed zero-cross circuit.

Have mains verified before replacing the motor control.

fixSteps.title: Measure supply
fixSteps.instruction: Have an electrician verify voltage and frequency.

fixSteps.title: Replace control
fixSteps.instruction: If supply is fine, swap motor control module.

faq.a: Only true-sine inverters with stable frequency.
